tour.overview:
Between Pisac and Ollantaytambo, the Urubamba river flows through a wide, fertile valley lined with snow-capped peaks, at about 2,800 metres, warmer and lower than Cusco. For the Incas it was the Sacred Valley, a granary of maize and the site of royal estates, temples and fortresses. Today Quechua farming communities still work the Inca terraces and weave textiles with techniques passed down for centuries.

This private day explores the valley with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the Inca citadel of Pisac and its market, have lunch, climb the terraces of Ollantaytambo, the only Inca town still lived in with its original layout, and learn about natural dyeing and weaving with a cooperative in Chinchero.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cusco or the Sacred Valley
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; many steps at Pisac and Ollantaytambo, at altitude

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Inca citadel of Pisac.
• The Pisac market.
• The fortress-temple of Ollantaytambo and the town.
• A weaving cooperative and the church of Chinchero.

WHY THIS WORKS
The valley is lower than Cusco, ideal for your first days of acclimatisation, and the car lets you see three sites at a relaxed pace.

WHO IT SUITS
First-time visitors to Cusco, families and anyone interested in Inca history and Andean culture.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you are short of time, end the day in Ollantaytambo and take the train to Machu Picchu from there.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The Boleto Turístico, a combined ticket for valley sites, is included. Pisac's market is busiest on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays. Weaving products are sold at the cooperative, with no obligation to buy.

days.name: Pisac ruins and market, lunch in the valley, Ollantaytambo and the weavers of Chinchero
days.description:
What to expect: the Inca sites and living culture of the Sacred Valley, with a licensed guide, private car, tourist ticket and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 8:00 and drive out of Cusco, past the viewpoint of Taray, down into the valley to Pisac. High above the town, the Inca citadel spreads across a mountain spur: sweeping curved terraces that follow the contours of the slope, a ceremonial centre with a sun temple, the Intihuatana, built of finely cut stone, residential quarters and, in the cliffs opposite, hundreds of holes that were Inca tombs. Your guide explains how the terraces created microclimates for different crops. You then walk through the Pisac market, where Quechua families sell fruit, vegetables, textiles and ceramics.

You drive along the valley, past fields of corn and villages, to Urubamba for a lunch of Andean dishes with a view of the mountains: quinoa soup, trout, alpaca, corn of giant kernels and local potatoes, of which Peru grows thousands of varieties.

In the afternoon you reach Ollantaytambo, the royal estate of the emperor Pachacuti and the site of the Incas' rare victory over the Spanish in 1536. You climb the steep terraces to the Temple of the Sun, where six enormous pink granite blocks, each weighing up to 50 tonnes, were dragged from a quarry across the river. Below, the town still follows its Inca grid, with water flowing in stone channels along the lanes. On the way back to Cusco you stop in Chinchero, a weaving village at 3,760 metres, where women of a cooperative show you how they wash alpaca wool with a root, dye it with plants, insects and minerals, and weave it on backstrap looms. You see the colonial church, built in 1607 on the walls of an Inca palace, with its painted ceiling. You are back at your hotel at about 18:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
09:00 – Pisac citadel.
11:00 – Pisac market.
13:00 – Lunch in Urubamba.
14:30 – Ollantaytambo.
16:30 – Chinchero weavers and church.
18:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Combine with Machu Picchu: we can drop you at Ollantaytambo station and arrange a night in the valley.
• Moray and the Maras salt mines can replace Chinchero.
• The altitude ranges from 2,800 to 3,760 metres; drink water and take it slowly.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, tourist ticket, weaving demonstration, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: purchases, drinks with lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the tourist ticket included?
faq.answer: Yes, the Boleto Turístico covering Pisac, Ollantaytambo and Chinchero.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, Andean dishes in Urubamba. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is it a good first day for acclimatisation?
faq.answer: Yes. The valley is lower than Cusco, and many travellers start their stay here.

faq.question: Can we continue to Machu Picchu?
faq.answer: Yes. We can end the day at Ollantaytambo station, with a night in the valley or the train to Aguas Calientes.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children enjoy the market, the llamas and the weaving. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Pisac and Ollantaytambo involve many steep steps; you can see much from the lower levels.

faq.question: Will we be pushed to buy textiles?
faq.answer: No. The cooperative sells its work, and buying supports the weavers, but there is no obligation.

faq.question: Will we be taken to commission shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers, sun protection, a hat, a rain jacket in the wet season and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October is dry and sunny; nights are cold. The rainy season is green, with afternoon showers.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
